result.headline: Pitch axis does not follow its setpoint (inverted, lagged response) while roll tracks; sensor-health error logged at t=1.264.
result.explanation: Pitch attitude is negatively correlated with its setpoint (-0.778 at 1.7 s lag), while roll follows with a 0.97 s lag. Pitch control path (sign, elevator channel, or attitude estimate) is leading; the data cannot say which.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=0 to 7.061 s (peak |error| 46.604 deg)
evidence.shows: Pitch diverged from the very start of the recording, before any actuator step.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=1.264 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor-health error was logged early, together with a low-voltage warning, but it is not tied to a particular sensor.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (1512 samples)
evidence.shows: The airspeed signal is dead for the whole flight; yaw_rate is also constant 0 (line 28).

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[2]] at t=6.419 s: 1164 -> 1604 us (step 440, 55x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The ch[2] step coincides with the throttle step (line 50) and the pitch setpoint step at 6.764 s (line 44), so it is probably a commanded response.

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs roll attitude relation
checked.result: Correlation 0.785 overall, 0.969 at 0.971 s lag; typical error 5.407 deg, worst 42.79 deg at 104.261 s. Roll follows its command with a delay.

checked.check: Pitch setpoint vs pitch attitude relation
checked.result: Correlation -0.55; -0.778 at 1.699 s lag. Typical error 5.708 deg, worst 46.604 deg at 3.829 s. The response is inverted.

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline in 0-12 s
checked.result: No signal left its baseline first; the only events are the battery warning and sensor-health error at 1.264 s. The earliest sign cannot be ordered because pitch is already diverged at t=0.

checked.check: Window 0-12 s on actuators, throttle and attitude
checked.result: Pitch stayed near 20-21 deg until ~6 s while ch[2] was 1116-1148 us, then ch[2] rose to 1676 and pitch fell to -10.8. ch[4] and ch[5] are identical (1400-1525).

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.altitude[relative] at t=5.548 s: 67.067 -> 49.111 m (step -17.955, 94x its usual variation)
effects.why: Altitude loss follows the pitch and throttle upset. It is a consequence, not a cause.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=41.23 s: -112.91 -> -188.771 deg (step -75.861, 146.6x its usual variation)
effects.why: Repeated yaw and velocity steps (lines 62-70) follow large roll and pitch setpoint reversals and look like manoeuvre effects.

next_action.action: Bench-test the pitch control chain with propellers removed
next_action.why: Separates a reversed pitch sign or wrong channel mapping from a faulty attitude estimate or sensor.
how: Props off, vehicle restrained. Tilt the airframe nose-up by hand and watch the reported vehicle.attitude[pitch] sign.
In stabilised mode, check which way the elevator surface moves and whether actuator.output[ch[2]] goes up or down.
Confirm the pitch servo direction and channel mapping against the airframe configuration.
Read the sensor-health status: IMU, baro and airspeed.
next_action.conditions: Bench, props off, battery fully charged, vehicle restrained, no flight.
next_action.baseline: Roll axis behaviour in the same test, and the same test on another healthy airframe.

outcomes.label: Elevator moves the wrong way
outcomes.means: The pitch sign or servo direction is inverted, which fits the inverted correlation.
outcomes.then: Review the configuration and mapping history for this airframe.

outcomes.label: Surface correct, attitude sign wrong
outcomes.means: The attitude estimate or IMU orientation is faulty.
outcomes.then: Request the raw IMU data and calibration.

outcomes.label: All correct on the bench
outcomes.means: The fault is dynamic or load dependent; the sensor-health error may be only a start-up artefact.

hypotheses.claim: Pitch command sign, servo direction or channel mapping is wrong or faulty, so pitch response is inverted.
hypotheses.because: Pitch correlation is -0.778 at a 1.7 s lag, while roll follows at +0.969. This is the only axis with an inverted response.

hypotheses.claim: The pitch attitude estimate is wrong because of the IMU or sensor fault flagged at start-up.
hypotheses.because: A sensor-health error is logged at 1.264 s and pitch is diverged from t=0, but no sensor is named.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage degrades actuators and thrust.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning is logged at 1.264 s, but no voltage signal exists in this recording.

hypotheses.claim: The roll channel responds late, about 0.97 s, and may be a separate lag problem.
hypotheses.because: Roll correlation is 0.969 at the best lag, so it tracks. Only the delay and large errors in manoeuvres remain.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed and yaw_rate are dead, so no airspeed feedback exists for control.
hypotheses.because: Both signals are constant 0 for the whole recording (lines 27-28). This is either a failure or a logging gap.
